Key points: - Rule options type includes Story-021 config flags (matching Implementation Notes): type TestTraceabilityOptions = { testFilePatterns?: string[]; requireDescribeStory?: boolean; requireTestReqPrefix?: boolean; describePattern?: string; autoFixTestTemplate?: boolean; // from story autoFixTestPrefixFormat?: boolean; // from story testSupportsTemplate?: string; // from story }; - Rule meta: - fixable: "code" (integrates with ESLint --fix as required) - Rule JSDoc includes explicit traceability for Story 021.0 and all its requirement IDs: * @supports docs/stories/021.0-DEV-TEST-ANNOTATION-AUTO-FIX.story.md REQ-TEST-FIX-TEMPLATE REQ-TEST-FIX-PREFIX-FORMAT REQ-TEST-FIX-SAFE REQ-TEST-FIX-PRESERVE REQ-TEST-FIX-PLACEHOLDER REQ-TEST-FIX-NO-INFERENCE - In create(context): - Determines test files via determineIsTestFile (non-test files ignored). - Calls ensureFileSupportsAnnotation(context, sourceCode, { autoFixTestTemplate, testSupportsTemplate }); → enforces and auto-fixes the file-level @supports template when missing. - Wires CallExpression visitor via handleCallExpression(context, { sourceCode, describeRegex, requireDescribeStory, requireTestReqPrefix, autoFixTestPrefixFormat }); → enforces and auto-fixes malformed [REQ-...] prefixes in it/test names.
3. Helper implementation directly matches story requirements: - buildSupportsTemplateComment(customTemplate?: string): - Default template value: "@supports docs/stories/XXX.X-STORY-NAME.story.md REQ-XXX-YYY REQ-XXX-ZZZ" - Produces: /** * @supports docs/stories/XXX.X-STORY-NAME.story.md REQ-XXX-YYY REQ-XXX-ZZZ * TODO: Replace the placeholder story path and REQ-IDs with real values for this test file. */ (followed by a blank line) - Satisfies: - File-Level Template (placeholder @supports comment) - Template Quality (clear TODO guidance) - REQ-TEST-FIX-TEMPLATE, REQ-TEST-FIX-PLACEHOLDER, REQ-TEST-FIX-NO-INFERENCE.
- insertSupportsTemplate(fixer, sourceCode, customTemplate?): - Preserves shebang lines by inserting after the first newline when text starts with "#!". - Otherwise inserts at the file start. - Ensures no change to executable semantics (REQ-TEST-FIX-SAFE, REQ-TEST-FIX-PRESERVE).
- ensureFileSupportsAnnotation(context, sourceCode, autoFixOptions): - Scans all comments for @supports. - If none found, reports messageId: "missingFileSupports". - If autoFixTestTemplate !== false, provides a fix that calls insertSupportsTemplate with optional custom template. - Only adds a non-semantic placeholder; never infers real story path or IDs.
- normalizeReqId(raw: string): - Trims and uppercases. - If not starting with "REQ", returns the input unchanged (no inference from arbitrary text). - For IDs starting with REQ, removes leading separators, converts spaces/underscores to hyphens, and collapses multiple hyphens. - E.g. "REQ_TEST_FIX" → "REQ-TEST-FIX"; "req-lowercase" → "REQ-LOWERCASE". - Satisfies REQ-TEST-FIX-PREFIX-FORMAT and REQ-TEST-FIX-NO-INFERENCE.
- normalizeReqPrefixInDescription(description: string): - If already canonical ([REQ-...]), returns null (no change). - Otherwise accepts and normalizes: - "[ REQ-XXX ] ..." → "[REQ-XXX] ..." (spacing) - "[REQ_XXX] ..." → "[REQ-XXX] ..." (underscore to dash) - "(REQ-XXX) ..." → "[REQ-XXX] ..." (parens to brackets) - "[req-xxx] ..." → "[REQ-XXX] ..." (case) - Returns null when no recognizable REQ identifier at the beginning, so no fix is applied when there is no prefix to normalize. - This is exactly the story’s “Malformed [REQ-XXX] prefix format” strategy and respects REQ-TEST-FIX-SAFE and REQ-TEST-FIX-NO-INFERENCE.
- createUpdatedStringLiteralRaw(originalNode, newValue, sourceCode): - Preserves the original quoting style and escapes appropriately. - Changes only the literal’s contained string, not surrounding code/formatting. - Supports REQ-TEST-FIX-PRESERVE (maintains formatting and indentation).
- handleItOrTestCall(context, node, description, options): - Requires REQ prefix when requireTestReqPrefix is true. - If description lacks canonical [REQ-...] prefix: - When autoFixTestPrefixFormat !== false, attempts normalization via normalizeReqPrefixInDescription. - Always reports messageId: "missingReqPrefix". - Only attaches a fix when: - autoFixTestPrefixFormat !== false, - normalizedDescription !== null (i.e. a recognizable REQ ID was present and normalized), and - the first argument is a string Literal. - If normalizedDescription is null (no recognizable REQ ID), reports an error but **no fix** → satisfies REQ-TEST-FIX-NO-INFERENCE and Safety criteria.

traceability.notes:
Every acceptance criterion from docs/stories/021.0-DEV-TEST-ANNOTATION-AUTO-FIX.story.md is implemented, tested, and documented:
- File-Level Template: Implemented by ensureFileSupportsAnnotation + buildSupportsTemplateComment + insertSupportsTemplate, inserting a JSDoc @supports block at the top of test files when missing. Tests verify the exact placeholder format and TODO line. - Format Fixes: Implemented by normalizeReqId + normalizeReqPrefixInDescription + handleItOrTestCall, which normalize malformed [REQ-...] prefixes (spacing, brackets vs parentheses, underscores, casing) only when a recognizable REQ token already exists. Tests cover each malformed pattern and confirm the expected fixed output. - Template Quality & User Experience: The default template contains explicit placeholder story path/REQ IDs and an explanatory TODO line, making it obvious what the developer must fill in. Tests assert this exact content; documentation explains the behavior. - Quality Standards & Safety: Auto-fixes are limited to comments and test name strings; test bodies and logic are untouched. Shebang handling preserves runnability; string literal rewriting preserves quote style and escapes. Cases without any REQ prefix receive diagnostics only, with no auto-fix applied, avoiding semantic guesses. - Integration: The rule is a first-class ESLint RuleModule with meta.fixable = "code" and is integrated into the plugin’s recommended/strict configs. It participates in normal ESLint --fix runs, as validated by the RuleTester tests and passing Jest suite. - Error Handling: For malformed but recognizable prefixes, the rule both reports an error and provides a safe fix; for unrecognized patterns (no REQ), it reports an error without a fix. For missing file-level @supports, it reports missingFileSupports and conditionally offers a fix depending on autoFixTestTemplate. - Documentation: The user API reference explicitly documents Story 021.0 auto-fix behavior and configuration (autoFixTestTemplate, autoFixTestPrefixFormat, testSupportsTemplate), including the safety constraints.
Given the concrete implementation in the rule and helpers, targeted tests that exactly match the story’s examples and requirements, and a fully passing test run, the story is fully implemented and satisfies all acceptance criteria.
